title: POC weekly sync - onboarding & env readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to review initial inference results, discuss tuning opportunities (batching, quantization), and confirm remaining access and environment readiness for Dedicated/private benchmarking. Action items created for VPC peering, security docs, and next demo for latency tuning.
topics: Next steps: scheduling in-region benchmarks and pilot ramp plan
transcript:
00:00 Jordan: okay uh hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, we have Priya on the SE side too. um we're gonna run through results and next steps.
00:12 Marta: hey hi, thanks, sorry running a bit late on our side, Ethan's on now.
00:19 Ethan: hey, sorry about that, laptop issues.
00:21 Priya: no worries. quick agenda - results from the hosted pilot, a couple tuning knobs, then access / environment readiness for the Dedicated run.
00:33 Jordan: quick housekeeping - recording and notes; we'll share the deck after. link: https://redwood.ai/deck/poc-nexahealth
00:41 Marta: great. on results - we ran the sample inference set and saw the average p50 latency at 140ms and p95 at 420ms on Redwood hosted. throughput is okay for our bursty use. we were expecting closer to 100ms p50 though.
01:00 Priya: got it, thanks Marta. a couple quick clarifications - what sequence length are you hitting in that test? and which model variant did you pick?
01:10 Marta: sequences around 512 tokens for longer docs, usually 256 for summaries, and we used the open-m-ntk-2-quant variant from the model catalog (we asked for quantized to save cost).
01:24 Priya: okay that explains some of it - quantized variants can add a bit of per-token latency depending on kernel path and your CPU/GPU mix. we can trade a bit of cost for lower p95 by switching to a better kernel selection or a different quant profile.
01:40 Ethan: can you explain the kernel thing again? we use GCP n1-standard with T4 right now for the Dedicated staging runs.
01:48 Priya: sure - Redwood's runtime picks kernels depending on model arch, sequence length, and hardware. on T4s with quantized weights sometimes we hit a suboptimal kernel for attention. we have a small tweak (we call it the "fast-attn" path) that benefits 256+ seqs, and we can enable that for your Dedicated pool during benchmarks.
02:05 Jordan: also worth noting prefix / KV cache - if you have repeated context we can enable prefix caching which reduces p50 significantly for repeated prompts.
02:15 Marta: we do have repeated blobs - customer metadata, and the beginning paragraphs repeated. that might help.
02:21 Priya: yes - enabling KV caching and bumping batch size slightly could move p50 to ~90-110ms in our estimates, p95 down to ~250-300ms, depending on concurrency.
02:33 Liam: quick security question - for Dedicated or Private, how do you handle KMS and audit logs? our compliance team is picky about key rotation and HSM-backed keys.
02:45 Jordan: good question - for Redwood Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and provide audit logs; we have a SOC 2 report and can share our security pack. we'll follow up with the detailed security docs and the SOC 2 PDF.
02:59 Marta: can you drop that now? we'll need it for our internal review.
03:03 Jordan: yes, will send. also the security pack link we'll share: https://redwood.ai/security/nexa-pack (placeholder).
03:10 Ethan: for the Dedicated benchmark, we need VPC peering and service account keys. our infra team is on PTO this week but should be back next Mon. what's the minimal access we need?
03:22 Priya: minimal - VPC peering + a service account with compute run permissions, and one port opened for the benchmark nodes. we can do a temporary test token for hosted-to-dedicated migration too.
03:34 Jordan: I'll put together a step-by-step access guide. also note our Dedicated requires a single bucket for model artifacts if you're bringing your own models.
03:44 Ethan: we're planning to bring our tuned model and also test one of Redwood's curated models. so we need that artifact flow set up.
03:51 Priya: perfect. for BYO model we also recommend running a short warmup trace to populate KV, and we can provide a trace runner script. I'll push that to the shared drive: drive.google.com/drive/folders/poc-nexa-benchmarks
04:06 Marta: cool. question on quantization - are you able to run int8 vs int4 comparisons? cost is a concern, but accuracy drop can't be more than 1.5% on our internal evals.
04:18 Priya: yes, we can run int8 vs int4. we usually run a quality regression matrix tied to your eval set. if int4 regresses >1.5% we can recommend int8 or hybrid quant profiles. we'll include that in the benchmarks spreadsheet.
04:31 Jordan: speaking of spreadsheets, here's the benchmark tracker we started: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/nexa-poc-benchmarks - we'll add the planned runs and expected metrics.
04:45 Ethan: timeline - we'd like Dedicated in our us-central region next Wed or Thu for an in-region run, is that feasible?
04:55 Jordan: next Wed might be tight but Thu doable; we need VPC peering set up and at least one service account by Tue EOD.
05:05 Marta: our infra comes back Mon, we can try to prioritize the peering.
05:10 Liam: compliance will need the SOC 2 and a diagram of network flows - does Redwood provide that?
05:17 Jordan: yes, we have an architecture diagram and flow docs. will attach to the security pack.
05:22 Marta: small note - during the earlier run we saw a couple of transcription artifacts in the logs (looks like tokenization differences) - could that affect reranking?
05:33 Priya: tokenization differences can slightly shift scores in reranking. we log tokenizer versions and can pin those in the runtime for consistency. recommend pinning the tokenizer and model version for the Dedicated run.
05:46 Ethan: on costs - can you give us an estimate of per-1M tokens on Dedicated with our expected throughput?
05:53 Jordan: ballpark - depends on instance type and quantization. for T4 with int8 we estimate $X per 1M tokens; int4 reduces compute but might add latency. I'll include a cost worksheet in the follow-up.
06:06 Marta: okay. next - any blockers for onboarding? on our side: infra availability next week, security review, and model artifact packaging.
06:16 Priya: from Redwood side: we need the model artifacts (S3/GCS link), VPC peering info, and confirm the model variant to test. we'll also need a list of eval prompts for the quality regression.
06:28 Jordan: adding to next steps - we'll send the onboarding checklist doc: https://redwood.ai/poc/onboarding-checklist (to be attached).
06:36 Marta: quick question about canary / fallback - if Dedicated has a transient outage, can requests fall back to hosted without data leakage?
06:46 Priya: yes - we support fallback to hosted variants with TLS and optional token scoping; data sent to hosted can be configured to avoid persistence, and we can enable per-route fallthrough policies. Liam, we can include details for your security review.
07:00 Liam: good, please include the non-persistence config and the retention policy.
07:07 Jordan: will do.
07:10 Marta: anything on monitoring? we saw a few spikes in error rates during the previous run.
07:15 Priya: our Console provides per-route latency and token-level cost breakdowns; for the bench we'll enable full tracing for a short window. we'll also add a couple of alerts for error rates >2%.
07:28 Ethan: perfect. on the actual Dedicated benchmark plan - can we run these jobs: warmup trace, int8 run, int4 run, and fallback test?
07:36 Priya: yes that sequence makes sense. warmup first to populate KV cache; then int8; then int4; then a configured fallback test for 10 minutes with induced network noise.
07:48 Jordan: I'll propose exact run durations in the benchmark tracker.
07:53 Marta: cool. any competitor comparisons to be aware of? our procurement asked about Anthropic and Vertex AI performance on similar workloads.
08:01 Jordan: we've done head-to-heads; in some latency cases Anthropic was close, Vertex has strong autoscaling but less opinionated inference optimizations. we'll include a short note in the follow-up.
08:12 Marta: thanks.
08:14 Priya: quick note - for the Dedicated pool config we'll recommend autoscale min=1, max=4 and a burst profile for prefetch to handle spikes; also suggest enabling prefix cache.
08:26 Ethan: sounds good.
08:28 Jordan: recap before we wrap - items to send: security pack + SOC2, onboarding checklist, access guide for VPC peering, benchmark tracker with proposed runs, cost worksheet, and the trace runner script.
08:42 Marta: and we'll prioritize getting infra back on Mon to setup peering.
08:46 Liam: we'll review security docs once you send.
08:49 Jordan: great. next call - propose Thu 10am CT for the in-region Dedicated run kickoff?
08:56 Marta: that works for us.
08:58 Jordan: awesome.
09:00 [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional filler words and small mis-attributions. some proper nouns (model names) may be slightly off in the transcript.
